subject: Food Science
title: Active and Smart Packaging
description: A quick, practical guide to Active and Smart Packaging.

hook.text: Some packaging absorbs oxygen, others release antimicrobials, and smart labels change color when food spoils.

buildup.text: Active packaging interacts with food or its environment: oxygen scavengers extend shelf life, ethylene absorbers slow fruit.

discovery.text: Iron-based oxygen absorbers in beef jerky packets remove residual oxygen, preventing fat oxidation and maintaining flavor for up.

twist.text: Time-temperature indicators (TTIs) on labels track cumulative heat exposure. They reveal if cold-chain was broken.

climax.text: Edible packaging made from seaweed or milk protein is being developed—you eat the wrapper.

punchline.text: Packaging that fights spoilage, reports abuse, and can be eaten.

quiz.question: What do time-temperature indicators (TTIs) on food packaging reveal?
options: Whether the cold-chain was broken—tracking cumulative heat exposure even after re-chilling
